answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable task bond before accepting work, with the bond size growing with the payout. New identities start with tiny, low-value jobs, like a reef that only shelters small fish at first; a gale of fake accounts cannot profit because each one must lock real funds and wait through slow, peer-reviewed work. If an agent cheats, its bond is slashed and its record marked, so the echo of one bad act follows that identity. Honest agents earn their bonds back quickly, making one trusted identity far cheaper than many disposable ones.
